name: Noddy
description: Noddy is a 16th-century English card game and the direct ancestor of Cribbage. It is the oldest identifiable card game with the Cribbage gaming structure. Played with a distinctive board for scoring, it features the familiar combination of pegging, fifteens, pairs, runs, and flushes that would later be refined into modern Cribbage.

history.origins: Noddy is the 16th-century English ancestor of Cribbage, making it the oldest identifiable card game with this gaming structure. It was played during the Tudor period in England. The game was described by David Parlett as the foundation from which Cribbage evolved.
timeline: 16th Century: Noddy played in Tudor England
Early 17th Century: Game evolves into Costly Colours
1630s: Sir John Suckling creates Cribbage by refining Noddy's rules
Present: Played by historical card game enthusiasts; preserved as Cribbage's predecessor
history.cultural: Part of Tudor English gaming culture. The game's survival through its descendant Cribbage makes it historically significant in the development of card games.
history.evolution: Noddy evolved into Costly Colours, which then influenced Sir John Suckling's creation of Cribbage in the 1630s. Cribbage refined Noddy's mechanics, adding the crib and modifying the scoring board. Noddy used four cards dealt (no crib) and was primarily a two-player game.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. In Noddy, Ace is low only (counts 1).
setup.dealing: Four cards dealt to each player (unlike Cribbage's six). No crib in Noddy.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, Noddy board (similar to Cribbage board but simpler), pegs for scoring.

rules.objective: Score points through card combinations (fifteens, pairs, runs, flushes) and be first to reach the target score (typically 31 or 61).
rules.gameplay: 1. Four cards dealt to each player. 2. Non-dealer cuts for starter card (turn-up). 3. Players alternately play cards to the pile, pegging points for fifteens, pairs, runs during play. 4. After all cards played, hands are counted for combinations. 5. Starter card applies to both hands.
keyRules: Starter card (turn-up) counts for both players' hands
Play to 31 without exceeding during pegging
Similar pegging and counting to Cribbage but simpler

strategy.basic: Similar to Cribbage strategy: try to make fifteens and pairs during play. Keep cards that work well together for the counting phase.
strategy.intermediate: Since there's no crib, focus entirely on your own hand strength. The starter card is crucialâ€”hands can change dramatically based on what turns up.
strategy.advanced: Card counting during play to predict opponent's holdings. Optimizing play order to maximize pegging opportunities while minimizing opponent's chances.
tips: Without a crib, you can play more aggressively in your hand construction
Ace is always 1â€”no 'one for his nob' equivalent for Ace
The simpler scoring means runs and fifteens are relatively more valuable
